name: Algeria
summary_text: Algeria is dangerous for trans visitors. Gender transition is not explicitly criminalised, but Cairo 52 documents that it is effectively criminalised through Penal Code Articles 333, 338, and 333 bis (indecency provisions), and NGOs have documented arrests of LGBT+ people under these articles. Same-sex activity itself carries up to 2 years under Article 338. There is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, and no visible community infrastructure — activism operates almost entirely underground. Unlike Tunisia or Morocco, Algeria lacks even a documented trans-visitor incident — partly because very few tourists visit and researchers have limited access. The legal exposure for a visibly trans visitor (indecency arrest) is real but the enforcement pattern is thinner than Egypt's entrapment machinery or Tunisia's 2024-25 arrest wave.

sources.title: Algeria | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Algeria: gender transition is not explicitly criminalised but is effectively criminalised under Articles 333, 338 and 333 bis ('indecency'); no legal framework for gender-affirming healthcare means doctors could be prosecuted under Articles 274/264; no legal gender recognition - a court denied a plaintiff's gender correction citing Sharia and Algerian societal norms.

UK Home Office Country Bulletin Algeria: Sexual orientation and gender identity or expression (July 2026): same-sex activity penalised under Article 338 (up to 2 years) and Article 333 'public indecency' (up to 3 years), applying to men and women; LGBT+ people are a particular social group; those fearing the state are unlikely to obtain protection or relocate internally.

sources.title: Algeria Prohibits Gender Transitions and Trans Identity? | Snopes.com
sources.claim_summary: Snopes fact check (Aug 2024): confirms the claim that Algeria prohibits gender transitions and trans identity - homosexuality is criminalised and gender-affirming medical/surgical care is not available; published during the Imane Khelif Olympic controversy.

sources.title: Algeria - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Algeria: official assessment including the SOGI section - Article 338 criminalises same-sex activity (up to 2 years), Article 333 'public indecency' (up to 3 years); documents arrests and prosecutions of LGBT people.
ILGA 'State-Sponsored Homophobia' world survey (May 2008): global survey of laws criminalising same-sex activity, with Algeria's entry (Articles 333 and 338 of the penal code).

sources.title: Algeria: Mass Convictions for Homosexuality | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Oct 2020): 'Algeria: Mass Convictions for Homosexuality' — 44 men convicted in a mass case in Constantine, with reports of abusive investigation.

sources.title: The Arab world in seven charts: Are Arabs turning their backs on religion?
sources.claim_summary: BBC (June 2019): 'The Arab world in seven charts' - Arab Barometer survey of 25,000+ people: acceptance of homosexuality is low or extremely low across the region (Lebanon 6%); rising irreligiosity among youth; Algeria was the exception on women's leadership acceptance - regional social-attitudes context.
